key_claims.claim: Quantitative MRI gyrification analysis detects cortical abnormalities in CMV-infected fetuses even when conventional MRI appears normal, with correlation to postnatal outcomes.
Incorporating fragment-size data into paired-end cfDNA sequencing reduces monosomy X screen-positive rate by 49% and trisomy X by 43% in a large screening population.
Congenital heart disease is associated with elevated maternal vascular malperfusion, and fetal vascular malperfusion increases specifically in CHD subtypes with reduced cerebral oxygenation.

In heterotaxy-CHD fetuses, complete heart block and ventricular dysfunction predict fetal demise; pulmonary venous obstruction and complete heart block predict postnatal mortality, with 68% 10-year survival.
A novel fetoscopic vesicostomy technique is proposed as an alternative intervention for fetal lower urinary tract obstruction.
